title: Fossil evidence favors a role for vision in the modular evolution of the primate neocortex.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file could be opened. Europe PMC core record confirms isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no cross-references and no text-mined accessions beyond RRID:SCR_026229 (which I resolved: it is Montana State University's Research Cyberinfrastructure computing cluster, not a dataset). The Science article page and both supplementary-file endpoints (doi/suppl/... and action/downloadSupplement?doi=...) returned HTTP 403. Dryad API searches for 'primate endocast neocortex', 'neocortex primate optic foramen' and the author names returned 0 matching records (the one endocast hit is an unrelated lagomorph paper). Zenodo search on the article code returned 0 records; figshare search returned no match. MorphoSource project API searches for this paper's title terms and author names returned no project for it. GitHub returned no repository for this paper (Chris Organ's six public repos are BayesTraits tooling, Canopy, a personal site, a COVID analysis, a variance-inflation helper and a phylogenetics setup; none is this study).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the data's contents comes from the abstract and press coverage only: virtual endocasts of extant and Eocene-Miocene fossil primates; volumes and surface areas of neocortical regions including the frontal lobe; optic foramen area as a proxy for visual input; micro-CT scans of skulls, many from the Duke Lemur Center Museum of Natural History. No specimen count, species count, units or table structure was found in any accessible source. I did not run the existing-models search because evaluation stopped at the first Part A failure, so the empty c2_audit means 'not searched', not 'searched and found nothing'.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. The paper is paywalled with no PubMed Central copy, and the Science supplementary-materials endpoints return HTTP 403 (and scraping publisher sites is out of scope). No deposit exists on Dryad, Zenodo, figshare, or as a MorphoSource project for this study. MorphoSource holds individual 3D media for some primate specimens, but nothing identifiable as this paper's measurement table.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not verifiable, and likely FAIL by construction. The quantities modelled (neocortex volume, frontal-lobe volume, non-frontal neocortex volume) are produced by manually segmenting virtual endocasts from micro-CT scans. If one worked from the 3D meshes on MorphoSource instead of the inaccessible table, the target would have to be built by hand-segmenting each endocast.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verifiable. No feature table was retrievable; CT volumes and surface meshes for the specimens are scattered across MorphoSource records that are not linked to this paper.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verifiable. Volumes are presumably cubic millimetres and optic foramen area square millimetres, but no file was opened to confirm, so this is inference, not a check.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not verified, and very likely FAIL. The analytical unit is a species or a specimen in a comparative phylogenetic study spanning extant primates plus Eocene-Miocene fossils; comparable endocast datasets run to roughly 100-250 rows, far under the ~1,500-row bar (or ~400 for classification). No count appears in the abstract, the press releases or any accessible source.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: under 0.1 GB for the measurement table; tens of GB if one re-segmented the raw micro-CT stacks
a6_fits_laptop.note: The measurement table, if it existed, would be trivially small. Re-deriving measurements from raw micro-CT scans would not fit the brief (raw imaging, large, and manual).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download to compare with the paper, and the paper itself is not readable.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is sound in principle: volumes come from physical micro-CT measurement of real skulls, not from another model's output. But body-mass estimates for fossils are themselves regression predictions, so any brain-size-relative label would partly inherit another model's output.

integration.partner_dataset: Could in principle join to the 10kTrees primate phylogeny or the PanTHERIA / Animal Diversity life-history database on species binomial name, and to MorphoSource on specimen catalogue number.
integration.join_key: species binomial (free text), museum specimen number
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written usefully: with no accessible measurement table there is nothing to join, and species names are free text rather than standard identifiers.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the textbook allometric scaling of brain volume on body mass, which any working pipeline must recover.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling across species, plus a phylogeny-shuffled control to confirm the signal is not just shared ancestry.
controls.external_validation: Stephan et al.'s classic histological primate brain-component volumes and published magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) comparative datasets measure overlapping quantities in living primates, so an external check would exist if the data were obtainable.

honest_claim_h3: Not assessed: evaluation stopped at the A1 failure. No honest claim can be stated for a dataset that cannot be opened.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use skull-cavity shape and eye-nerve-hole size to predict how big each brain region was in extinct primates.
plain_idea.train_on: Measurements from virtual casts of the inside of primate braincases (endocasts) made from micro-CT scans: total braincase volume, optic foramen area (the bony hole the optic nerve passes through), and estimated body mass. Number of specimens: unknown, no count found anywhere accessible.
plain_idea.predict: The volume of individual neocortical regions (frontal lobe versus occipital, parietal and temporal regions). The true answer comes from the authors manually segmenting each 3D endocast using the impressions sulci leave on the braincase wall.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Palaeoanthropologists usually recover fragmentary skulls where some regions are crushed; a model that infers regional brain proportions from the parts that survive would let them place more fossils in the comparative record. Even a failure would quantify how much regional brain structure is predictable from braincase size alone.

ml_idea: Considered: predict regional neocortex volumes (frontal versus non-frontal) and optic foramen area from overall endocast size, body mass and phylogenetic position, to impute brain organisation for fragmentary fossils. Rejected because no data file is obtainable and the species-level sample size is an order of magnitude below the minimum.

effort.compute_note: No estimate possible: no file was retrievable, so nothing was timed or measured. If the supplementary table were released it would be a few hundred kilobytes and any model would fit in seconds.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the paper's specimen table. If it has fewer than ~400 species or specimens, which comparable endocast studies strongly suggest, the project is dead regardless of access.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: paywalled Science paper with no PubMed Central copy, supplementary-file endpoints return HTTP 403, and no deposit exists on Dryad, Zenodo, figshare, MorphoSource or GitHub. A5 almost certainly fails too - the unit is a primate species or specimen in a comparative endocast study, which means hundreds of rows at most - and the regional brain volumes are produced by manual segmentation rather than existing as a ready column (A2).
